items.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
items.q: he played with us out on Long Island, come out a couple of times, and played with us, just for fun of it.

ctx.x: Maybe get more emotional impact. I guess so, I guess so. Do you think Bache was mainly flat?

Well, it just seemed like it never seemed to be in tune to me. To me, he just never, he played with us out on Long Island, come out a couple of times, and played with us, just for fun of it. Of course, one time, I was playing in Long Island, Jeff Bache was, wasn't doing so good, he'd open up a place, a gambling place, and he'd lost all his money. He'd had money once, but he was broke at that time. And I don't know, I'd heard the guy play clarinet before, and just to me, maybe I was prejudiced. I'd heard him play…
Well, he didn't play the clarinet out of tune as he did the soprano. Or you didn't notice it? No. I didn't know it. To me, he's just a natural kind of player. Just natural.
